title: Topic
description: One word-list topic (a single file; entries carry their own per-language forms). See docs/archive/PLANNING.md §4.

id.description: Kebab-case topic id; matches the topic's folder name (foldered) or file stem (flat).

title.description: Display name, in the same shape as an entry: a plain string where the name is global ("South Park"), a language map where it translates ({ "en": "SpongeBob SquarePants", "de": "SpongeBob Schwammkopf" }), or a short/long pair — the app puts `short` on the row and `long` in a hover, so a long name needn't crowd the tree.

languages.description: Languages this topic fully supports. The frontend flags a topic (⚠️) when the selected language isn't listed — including when this field is omitted (support undeclared, shown even for English). Declare the languages to confirm support, including for a language-neutral list whose entries read the same in every locale.

usesEnglishFor.description: Languages in which this list deliberately uses the English names, because that is what they are called there (League of Legends champions in German, Pokémon in any locale Nintendo never localized). The frontend shows ℹ️ instead of nothing, so a reader seeing English words knows it is intentional. Normally a subset of `languages`, which stays the complete list of supported languages. `"*"` stands for every language not named in `languages` and is the one member that cannot also appear there.

hideRulersByDefault.description: When true, this topic's fame ruler starts hidden behind a toggle rather than shown — useful for a flat list whose ruler is just its checkbox (e.g. one Pokémon generation). Declaring the field (either value) also makes the topic its own ruler-visibility boundary, so no ancestor category's toggle flips it. Omitted: inherited from the nearest ancestor that declares it, else shown.

sources.description: Where the entries came from — one string or a list of them. Free-form, so a label can precede the link ("German: https://…"); validate-data warns when an item contains no URL.

generatedRomaji.description: True when this list's romaji were produced by transliterating its Japanese names rather than taken from a source that names them — see src/lib/kana.ts. A reading derived from kana is correct as a reading and may still not be how the name is officially spelled in Latin script, so the UI says where that is the case and invites a correction.

order.description: Where this sits among its siblings, lowest first. Undeclared sorts last, alphabetically — so ordering a few of them needs nothing on the rest. The tree is otherwise the file system's, which puts Animation first and Gaming sixth for no reason anyone chose.

corrections.description: Where the source is simply wrong, and what the right name is. An instruction to the IMPORT, not to the app: unlike an omission — which describes how a list should be shown and is applied on every load — a correction is baked into the entry, and this field exists only so the next re-import does not undo it. The frontend never reads it.

entry.description: The entry this corrects, by its English name — the identity every list is keyed by. Named `entry` rather than `en` so that English itself can be corrected like any other language.

why.description: What the source gets wrong. Plain text, not localized: a note to whoever re-runs the import, never shown to a reader.

^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2}|-[0-9]{3}|-[A-Z][a-z.description: One language's repair. `new` is what the entry must carry, so validate-data can tell when a re-import has quietly undone it. `old` is what the source said when the correction was written: an import that finds something else has hit an upstream change, and must stop rather than overwrite it — the source may have fixed the bug, or renamed the thing for a reason of its own.

credits.description: Who compiled or curated this list — one string or a list of them. Free-form: a name, a handle, an issue link.

lastUpdated.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the list's contents last actually changed.

lastChecked.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the list was last verified against its source (even if unchanged). Lets us spot which lists are due for a currency re-check.

stringOrList.description: A single string, or a list of them when there is more than one.

langMapString.description: A per-language string: keys are language codes ("en" is the required base), values the localized text. Languages that match "en" are omitted.

locString.description: A string that is the same everywhere (plain string) or translates (language map).

namePair.description: An entry with a short (common) and long (full) name; the UI's per-group Names dropdown picks short / long / both. Each field may itself be a language map when only that part translates — the preferred form.

langMapEntry.description: An entry-level per-language map: keys are language codes ("en" is the base), values are whole entries (a string or a name pair). Equivalent in content to leaf-localizing each field; the leaf form is preferred, but this whole-entry form is accepted too (e.g. from community content).

?.description: Languages this entry has NO name in — the source data carried none. Not the same as an absent key, which means the language agrees with "en": without this, a bulk source that stops localizing partway would silently assert the English word as the German one. Written by the enrichment scripts, and outranked by an own key for the same language, so a name filled in by hand needs no edit here.

omission.description: One family of entries left out of a list, and why. Every rule can be switched back on by the reader, from the panel that lists them.

id.description: Stable key for the reader's stored choice, unique within the group — the glob may be edited without resetting it.

match.description: Whole-name glob, or a list of them when one family is named too differently across languages to share a pattern (`X-Angriff 2` vs. `Angriffplus2`): `*` any run, `?` one character, `[0-9]` a class. Globs rather than regexes because these are hand-written in JSON, where a regex would need doubled backslashes and anchors in every rule. An entry matches when ANY of its language forms does — the same junk is named differently per language ("Data Card 01" / "Datenkarte01"), so one rule per family suffices, written in whichever language reads best.

reason.description: Why they are out, in one phrase — the line beside the checkbox that can bring them back, so write it for the reader. Localized here rather than in a locale file because it describes this list's source, not the app: adding a word list never means editing en.ts. May carry `{br}` and `[text](url)` links (https only), resolved by src/locale/html.

as.description: A name that stands for the whole family, added to the list in their place. For a family whose base form the source never had: `Datenkarte01`…`27` collapse to `Datenkarte`. Leave it out where the base form is already an entry of its own (the `X-… 2`–`6` variants). A stand-in joins the least famous tier, since it represents a family pruned for being obscure.

except.description: Names the glob catches but shouldn't. A glob has no negation, and one exception is cheaper than a pattern contorted to avoid it: `*-Bonbon` means the 80 species candies, not `Dynamax-Bonbon`. Compared against any language form, like the glob itself.

locked.description: When true, the reader can't switch this rule off: the panel shows its checkbox disabled. For a family that isn't words at all, where re-including it could only be an accident — the 300 Dynamax Crystals named `★Sgr6879` after Bright Star Catalogue entries. Rare by design: the default is that anything omitted can be asked back.

group.description: A subtopic; the smallest checkbox unit. Carries exactly one of `words` (flat) or `tiers` (fame-ordered).

title.description: Display name, same shape as a topic's.

omitted.description: Families of entries this list hides from its source — junk nobody could draw, or numbered copies of one drawable thing. The entries stay in the file and are filtered on the way into the list, so a rule is always reversible and the ⌗ panel can say what was left out.

omittable.description: Families the list OFFERS to leave out: same shape as `omitted`, opposite default. Present unless the reader ticks them off — for entries that are legitimate words but the first thing someone short of drawing room would cut (the 80 species candies). Rule ids must be unique across both arrays.

tiers.description: Ordered fame tiers, tier 0 = most famous; order within a tier is irrelevant.

preset.description: A named bundle of group ids (e.g. "Include all").

groups.description: References to group ids in this topic; referential integrity is checked by validate-data, not the schema.
